messages:
ciara: heads-up — onboarding Sherpa (customer) LoRA merge is mostly green but we see weird token aliasing when we run int4 builds. Quick thread to triage.
ciara: steps: merged LoRA into base-7b, quantized to int4 using our autotune profile, ran quickpack (50 prompts). several prompts show truncated entity mentions (e.g., 'SherpaCorp' -> 'Sherpa' + wrong casing).
maya: can you paste an example input/output?
sam: :thinking: could be tokenizer vocab difference after merge or kv-cache alignment after quantization. both plausible.
ciara: example below (raw):
```
INPUT: "Write a short blurb introducing SherpaCorp's new API for payments."
OUTPUT (gold): "SherpaCorp's new payments API helps teams..."
OUTPUT (int4): "Sherpa's new payments API helps teams..."
```
ciara: noticed the model drops the 'Corp' suffix or merges it with next token sometimes. not random — consistent across runs for a subset of prompts.
andre: did you try running the same model in fp16 without quant? to rule out merge artifact vs quant artifact.
ciara: yes — fp16 merge (same LoRA weights, no quant) matches gold. issue only shows after int4 compile.
maya: please run tokenizer.encode on the prompt before/after merge to inspect token ids. often LoRA merges with a different tokenizer config or causes subtle token id remap if tokenizers cached differently.
ciara: ran quick compare:
```
# after base load (fp16)
encode("SherpaCorp") -> [12034, 987]
# after merged LoRA + int4 compile
encode("SherpaCorp") -> [12034, 987]
# BUT model.generate seems to prefer splitting into [12034, 13, 987] in decoding beam for int4 build
```
ciara: so tokenizer returns same ids, but generation probabilities shift toward inserting an extra small token id (13) between pieces.
sam: OK that screams of quant-decoding bias. int4 kernel rounding can push logit gaps so that a short glue-token (comma/space variant) becomes higher-prob. can you diff top-k logits for the relevant step?
ciara: attaching quick log snippet from the inference trace (small table):
```
step t: logits top5 for prefix 'Sherpa' (fp16): [45:0.42, 987:0.31, 13:0.01, 12034:0.00, 999:0.00]
step t: logits top5 for prefix 'Sherpa' (int4): [45:0.35, 13:0.33, 987:0.20, 12034:0.01, 999:0.00]
```
ciara: so int4 bumped token 13 (a small-space/soft punctuation) up significantly.
maya: can you point to which kernel config you used during compile? maybe try our alternate quant-block (preserve-high-precision-heads) flag. that one keeps attention heads in fp16 for the first N layers. sometimes fixes early decoding artifacts.
ciara: current compile flags: `--quant int4 --autotune-profile=balanced --preserve-embeds=false`. i'll recompile with `--preserve-high-precision-heads=4` and rerun.
ops-bot: smoke test started for model sherpalo-merge-int4-phh4 at 5862341205 (runs: quickpack-50).
ciara: ran PHH4 build — initial quickpack looks better: fewer insertions but still 6/50 prompts show subtle suffix drop.
andre: how about trying KV-cache alignment test? sometimes quant-packed KV tile sizes round differently and shift positional bias for suffix tokens. run the regen-with-prefix test: generate with growing prefix and check marginal prob of token sequence.
ciara: did regen-with-prefix, results: marginal prob of token id 987 (the 'Corp' piece) drops by 18% at decode step N in int4 vs 2% in fp16.
sam: that magnitude is notable. two orthogonal mitigations: 1) keep embeddings/last lm-head in fp16 (`--preserve-embeds=true`) or 2) apply small calibrated bias-correction on logits for those token ids (we have a quickpatch that adds a learned delta from evalset).
maya: we should run the calibrated delta on the Sherpa quickpack and check BLEU/ROUGE/instr-follow deltas. if it fixes, it's lower-risk than forcing more fp16 and raising latency.
ciara: ran quick calibrate: used 200 prompt pairs, learned delta vector for 150 token ids, applied at decode. metrics:
```
metric | fp16 baseline | int4 (no patch) | int4 + calib-delta
instr-acc | 0.93 | 0.78 | 0.91
exact-match (org names) | 0.97 | 0.82 | 0.95
avg latency (1k tokens) | 240ms | 95ms | 100ms
```
ciara: so calibrated delta recovers most of quality, latency stays near int4.
andre: nice. do we have concerns about overfitting the delta to Sherpa prompts? could cause regressions on other customers if used globally.
maya: keep it per-customer / per-variant behind routing policy. Redwood supports model-variant pinning for a tenant. we can ship sherpalo-merge-int4-calib as a customer-specific variant.
sam: one more ask — add a small unit test in our eval harness that asserts name-preservation for customer-defined entities. puts quickpack guard on future quant changes.
ciara: opened PR with quickpack additions + eval artifact link: https://redwood.internal/evals/sherpa/5862341120/pack-200.
ciara: next steps I propose: 1) deliver int4 + calib patch variant to Sherpa (staging) 2) run longer soak (2k prompts) overnight 3) if stable, include variant in Dedicated pool routing for their tenant.
maya: sounds good. can I take ownership of the soak overnight?
ciara: assigned to maya. thanks all :white_check_mark:
